# Revert auto-generated docstrings for FFI fields/methods to fix Sphinx compatibility
## TL;DR
- Reverts the auto-generated default docstring behavior introduced in PR #49 for `TypeField.as_property` and `TypeMethod.as_callable`.
- Docstrings are now only attached to FFI fields and methods when explicitly provided via `ObjectDef<T>` registration (e.g., `def_ro("a", &Obj::a, "Field \`a\`")`).
- Adds a regression test verifying that explicitly provided docstrings are propagated correctly.

## Key Exports

The public API surface is unchanged. The behavioral change is internal to `TypeField.as_property` and `TypeMethod.as_callable`:

```python
@dataclasses.dataclass(eq=False)
class TypeField:
    name: str
    doc: str | None  # None when no docstring provided in C++ ObjectDef
    # ...

    def as_property(self, cls: type) -> property:
        # Before (PR #49): always set doc, defaulting to "{module}.{qualname}.{name}"
        # After (this fix): only set doc/fget.__doc__/fset.__doc__ when self.doc is not None
        # Invariant: property.__doc__ is None when no docstring registered in C++
        # Interacts with: Sphinx autodoc (reads property.__doc__ to generate docs)
        ...

@dataclasses.dataclass(eq=False)
class TypeMethod:
    name: str
    doc: str | None
    # ...

    def as_callable(self, cls: type) -> Callable:
        # Before (PR #49): always set func.__doc__, defaulting to "Method `{name}` of class `{qualname}`"
        # After (this fix): only set func.__doc__ when self.doc is not None
        # Invariant: func.__doc__ is None when no docstring registered in C++
        # Interacts with: Sphinx autodoc
        ...
```

## Impact
- API: none -- no signature changes
- Behavioral: Properties and methods without explicit C++ docstrings now have `__doc__ = None` instead of auto-generated placeholder strings. This restores Sphinx autodoc compatibility (Sphinx treats `None` docstrings differently from non-empty placeholder strings).
- Flags/config: none
- Data formats/schemas: none

## Design Elements
Design elements this commit consumes:
- **TypeField.as_property / TypeMethod.as_callable** ([0015-ffi-python-type-system](../design-records/0015-ffi-python-type-system.md)) -- the two methods where docstring attachment is fixed.
- **ObjectDef<T>.def_ro** ([0007-ffi-reflection](../design-records/0007-ffi-reflection.md)) -- C++ reflection builder that optionally takes a docstring parameter (third argument to `def_ro`).

Design elements this commit produces: None -- restores pre-PR#49 behavior without introducing new elements.

## Usage Examples
Before/after pattern showing the bug and fix:

```python
# C++ registration with explicit docstring:
#   refl::ObjectDef<TestIntPairObj>()
#       .def_ro("a", &TestIntPairObj::a, "Field `a`")
#       .def_ro("b", &TestIntPairObj::b, "Field `b`")

import tvm_ffi

obj = tvm_ffi.testing.TestIntPair(3, 4)

# Explicit docstrings are preserved:
assert type(obj).a.__doc__ == "Field `a`"
assert type(obj).b.__doc__ == "Field `b`"

# Fields WITHOUT explicit docstrings now have __doc__ = None
# (previously PR #49 generated "module.qualname.name" placeholder)
# This is what Sphinx expects for undocumented attributes.
```
